name: United States
rationale: Diffuse dry agricultural residues, moderate nutrient status, good geologic storage access (nearest qualifying storage ~815 km) -> with proximate geologic storage, Vaulted-style slurry injection is cheaper on balance than bio-oil for these residues and removes more carbon (>89% CDR efficiency): raw biomass is injected at nearby wells rather than pyrolyzed to densify it for long-haul transport. Bio-oil overtakes only as wells get more distant.
caveats: National rollup -- feedstock type/density, storage access, and nutrient status vary substantially sub-nationally; the optimal pathway is local. See US state-level cells for spatially-resolved recommendations.
flags: Corn-ethanol+CCS excluded by Frontier (food/land competition, marginal additionality, thesis exclusions); not recommended despite local ethanol capacity.

name: Canada
rationale: Diffuse woody forestry residues, moderate nutrient status, good geologic storage access (nearest qualifying storage ~878 km) with a retrofittable pulp_paper anchor (West Fraser Hinton Pulp Mill) -> BECCS retrofit of existing pulp & paper / bioenergy maximizes CDR efficiency (80%) plus energy co-product -- Frontier's top-preferred use of biomass.
caveats: National rollup -- feedstock type/density, storage access, and nutrient status vary substantially sub-nationally; the optimal pathway is local.

name: Mexico
rationale: Diffuse dry agricultural residues, moderate nutrient status, moderate geologic storage access (~840 km) -> diffuse residues distant from concentrated storage favor modular bio-oil sequestration (Charm-style roving model, ~45% CDR efficiency) returning biochar + nutrients.
